facts.text: Father William says the black dragon can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Brandon in Brandon's Barrow Mound; the party could retrieve it from the Barrow.

classification.support_basis: George says nothing pierces the dragon's scales and only Brandon ever killed it, so the sword may be the decisive means of killing it, though George says no one knows what is true or where the sword is.
classification.action_basis: The Barrow's location is known and marked on the party's map, and the party has set out to walk there.
classification.opening_basis: A specific weapon said to be the only thing able to kill the dragon lies at a known site; retrieving it overcomes the dragon's unpierceable scales, an advantage beyond simply confronting the dragon.

facts.resource_subject: Brandon's sword as the only way to kill the dragon

facts.text: Father William marked Brandon's Barrow Mound on the party's map; it is roughly a three-mile walk north through the forest.

classification.support_basis: Knowing where the Barrow is lets the party reach the sword without searching for it.

facts.resource_subject: Location and distance of Brandon's Barrow Mound

facts.text: Is Brandon's magic sword really buried in the Barrow Mound?

classification.grounding_justification: Father William says the sword is buried with Brandon, while George says the tale is a fairytale and no one knows what's true or where the sword is.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Visiting the Barrow would largely settle it in one discovery.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental, though it bears on the legend of Brandon.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Farmer Gill's fairytales and the Barrow itself offer some leads, but a visit would mostly settle it.

facts.text: George says Farmer Gill knows the fairytales about Sir Brandon and his sword; the party could ask Gill what the tales say about the sword.

classification.support_basis: The tales might clarify what the sword is and whether it is at the Barrow, though they are fairytales of doubtful truth.
classification.action_basis: Gill is friendly with Dunk and George names him as knowing the tales; asking him is a simple conversation.
classification.opening_basis: A named source of the Brandon legend could give information about the sword before the party reaches the Barrow.
